b: Walk down Pink Street in Lisbon’s Cais do Sodré and you’ll eventually find a door that looks like it has secrets. Pensão Amor building is a former brothel that has been transformed into a surprising space in Lisbon's port district.

Cais do Sodré was once the sailors’ quarter, where seamen fresh off the boats mingled with writers, fado singers, artists, prostitutes and the occasional spy. Pensão Amor takes that cast of characters and gives them a party.

The bar is a riot of velvet, red light, and cheerful mischief. On any given night, you might catch burlesque, pole dancing, live music, poetry, or theater, sometimes all in the same week. Nobody here is trying to hide what the building used to be. They hung it on the wall.

Other surprise is upstairs. In 2023, the old brothel floors reopened as Madam’s Lodge, a 22-room hotel with a twist: every room has its own invented backstory. Screenwriter and director Roger Mor wrote each one, drawing on archival research and objects tied to the building and the neighborhood.

Illustrator Nuno Saraiva drew the characters and left his mark across the building, so even the walls seem to have opinions. Some rooms also come with pole dancing bars, strategically placed mirrors, bathtubs made for two, and minibars stocked with adult goodies.
